title: Harbhajan Singh v. Manjit Kaur
text: This first appeal arises from a decree of eviction passed by the Rent Controller against the tenant, Manjit Kaur. The landlord, Harbhajan Singh, sought eviction on grounds of personal necessity and non-payment of arrears of rent under the Punjab Rent Act. The tenant pleaded that she is a protected tenant and that her tenancy is protected under the Rent Control Act. The appellate court examined the evidence. The landlord's bona fide need for personal use of the premises was established through affidavit and medical certificates showing old age. The arrears of rent for 18 months remained unpaid despite notices. The defence of protected tenant was not substantiated. The court upholds the eviction decree. The tenant is granted six months' time to vacate the premises. Arrears of rent shall be paid before possession is handed over. The landlord succeeds in the eviction petition.
